whatItIs.text: Milk curdled with rennet or acid, then drained, salted, and often aged; more than a thousand types exist, from fresh to hard aged wheels.

historyNote.text: Cheesemaking may go back to around 8000 BC with the first sheep domestication; the earliest archaeological evidence is milk-fat-coated strainers from Kuyavia, Poland, dated to 5500 BC.

howToChoose.text: Buy from the back of the counter where stock rotates, check the date for fresh cheeses, and for aged cheeses a little rind character is normal while ammonia smells are not.

storage.text: Wrap in waxed or cheese paper rather than clingfilm and keep in the warmest part of the fridge; the rulebook has the windows and when-to-trim guidance.

foodSafetyRef.note: storage windows and mould guidance live in the food-safety rulebook

useItUp.text: Odd ends melt into sauce, toast, or a fromage forté blended with a splash of wine; rinds flavour soups and stocks.

substitutions.note: match texture, not name: mozzarella for stretch, cheddar for flavour
